key_insight: The paper replaces hand-tuned constraint penalties with a hardware-aware quadratic projection that best fits a chosen non-quadratic penalty under Walsh–Fourier least squares on the target QUBO connectivity graph.
engineering_relevance: This reduces penalty tuning, respects annealer hardware couplings, and can lower embedding overhead and chain lengths for more practical near-term quantum optimization.
method: Choose a constraint-matching penalty function, often non-quadratic (e.g., a Heaviside surrogate).
Project it onto the linear and quadratic Walsh–Fourier basis allowed by the hardware graph using weighted least squares.
Use the resulting quadratic surrogate directly as a slack-free QUBO, avoiding dense all-pairs couplings and per-constraint penalty coefficients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical evaluation showing the hardware-native surrogate outperforms denser full-pairwise projections and, after embedding and annealing, yields the lowest worst-case and mean objective gaps versus baseline penalization schemes.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen penalty function and target hardware graph, so the surrogate quality may degrade if the constraint is poorly represented or the device connectivity is very limited.
paper_title: Hardware-Aware QUBO Reformulation of Constrained Binary Optimization via the Walsh-Fourier Transform
